source: MemBrain in-domain set: 36 synthetic enterprise notes, 48 hand-labelled queries (written before any results were seen)

docs.title: Postmortem: checkout outage on March 14
docs.body: Between 09:12 and 10:05 UTC customers could not complete payments. The root cause was an expired TLS certificate on the payments gateway load balancer; renewal had been manual and the reminder email went to a former employee. We restored service by issuing a new certificate. Follow-ups: automate renewal with cert-manager, alert 30 days before expiry, and add the gateway to the synthetic monitoring suite.

docs.title: Postmortem: search latency spike (INC-2291)
docs.body: Search p95 latency rose from 180 ms to 2.4 s for forty minutes after the 2.18 release. A new filter disabled the use of the HNSW index, forcing sequential scans over the chunks table. Rolling back the release fixed it. Action items: add an EXPLAIN check to CI for the search query and a latency SLO alert at 500 ms.

docs.title: Decision: move the data warehouse from Redshift to Snowflake
docs.body: After a three-month evaluation the data platform team chose Snowflake over staying on Redshift. Main reasons: separation of storage and compute, so finance reporting no longer competes with ad-hoc analytics, and per-second billing. Priya owns the migration; the cutover target is the end of Q2. dbt models will be ported first, then Looker dashboards.

docs.title: Decision: standardise on PostgreSQL for new services
docs.body: New backend services will use PostgreSQL unless there is a documented reason not to. MongoDB stays for the legacy catalogue service until it is rewritten. Rationale: one operational skill set, strong transactional guarantees, and pgvector covers our semantic search needs without a separate vector database.

docs.title: SOP: on-call escalation
docs.body: If a customer-facing error rate exceeds 2% for five minutes, the primary on-call engineer acknowledges the page within 5 minutes. If the incident is not mitigated within 15 minutes, escalate to the secondary and open an incident channel named inc-<date>-<service>. SEV1 incidents require an incident commander and status page updates every 30 minutes.

docs.title: SOP: production database access
docs.body: Direct production database access requires an approved request in the access portal and is granted for at most four hours through the bastion host. All sessions are recorded. Read-only replicas should be used for investigations; write access needs a second approver from the database reliability team.

docs.title: SOP: rotating API credentials
docs.body: Service API keys are rotated every 90 days. Generate the new key in Vault, deploy it alongside the old one, confirm traffic has moved using the key-usage dashboard, then revoke the old key. Never paste credentials into tickets or chat; if that happens, rotate immediately and report it to security.

docs.title: Sprint 42 planning
docs.body: Committed: billing revamp phase 1 (invoice PDF redesign, proration fixes), the SSO login bug for Okta tenants, and dark mode for the dashboard. Deferred: CSV export improvements. Capacity is reduced because two engineers are on leave. The team agreed to timebox the proration work to five days.

docs.title: Q3 hiring plan
docs.body: Engineering will open four roles in Q3: two backend engineers for the payments team, one SRE, and one data engineer to support the warehouse migration. Interview loops use the new structured rubric. The mobile hire is postponed to Q4 because the iOS rewrite was descoped.

docs.title: Customer call: Acme Corp renewal
docs.body: Acme Corp is happy with the product but threatened not to renew unless audit logs are exportable to their SIEM. Their security team uses Splunk. We promised a Splunk integration by September; account owner is Daniel. They also asked about data residency in the EU.

docs.title: Customer call: Globex onboarding issues
docs.body: Globex reported that new users never receive invitation emails. Investigation showed their mail gateway rejects messages from our transactional email provider because SPF was misconfigured on our sending subdomain. Fixed by adding the provider to the SPF record; Globex confirmed invites now arrive.

docs.title: Architecture review: event bus
docs.body: We reviewed replacing direct service-to-service HTTP calls for order events with an event bus. Kafka was rejected as too heavy to operate for our volume; we will use managed Google Pub/Sub. Consumers must be idempotent because delivery is at-least-once. Owner: Marcus. A spike will measure end-to-end latency.

docs.title: Retro: mobile app release 5.0
docs.body: What went well: feature flags let us ship dark launches safely. What went badly: the App Store review took nine days because of a missing privacy manifest, which delayed the marketing campaign. Action: add App Store privacy requirements to the release checklist and submit builds a week earlier.

docs.title: Security review: file upload feature
docs.body: The new attachment upload accepts PDFs and images. Findings: file type was checked only by extension, uploads were stored in a public bucket, and there was no size limit. Required before launch: validate magic bytes, move storage to a private bucket with signed URLs, cap uploads at 10 MB, and scan files with ClamAV.

docs.title: Error runbook: ERR_PAYMENT_DECLINED_51
docs.body: Error code 51 from the card processor means insufficient funds. It is not a system fault: show the customer a retry-with-another-card message and do not trigger an alert. A sudden spike in code 51 across many customers can indicate a processor-side issue and should be raised with the processor's support.

docs.title: Error runbook: OOMKilled pods in the worker deployment
docs.body: Worker pods restarting with OOMKilled usually means a large document export loaded the whole file into memory. Short term, raise the memory limit to 2 GiB. Long term, stream exports in chunks. Check the export queue length in Grafana before scaling up replicas.

docs.title: Vendor evaluation: feature flag platform
docs.body: We compared LaunchDarkly, Unleash and building our own. LaunchDarkly has the best SDKs but costs roughly 40k per year at our seat count. Unleash self-hosted meets requirements and fits our Kubernetes setup. Recommendation: Unleash, with a review after six months.

docs.title: Policy: remote work and core hours
docs.body: Employees may work remotely up to four days a week. Core collaboration hours are 11:00 to 15:00 local time, when meetings should be scheduled. Each team holds one in-person day per month. Equipment stipends are 500 per year.

docs.title: Policy: expense reimbursement
docs.body: Expenses must be submitted within 30 days with a receipt. Conference travel needs manager approval in advance. Meals while travelling are covered up to 60 per day. Software purchases go through IT procurement rather than personal cards.

docs.title: Onboarding checklist for engineers
docs.body: Day one: laptop setup, SSO, GitHub access, and the security training. Week one: run the monorepo locally, ship a small fix behind a feature flag, and shadow an on-call shift. Each new hire gets an onboarding buddy for the first month.

docs.title: Design doc: rate limiting for the public API
docs.body: Public API clients will be limited per API key using a token bucket: 100 requests per second burst, 20 per second sustained. Limits are enforced at the gateway with Redis counters. Clients receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Enterprise plans can request higher limits.

docs.title: Design doc: multi-region failover
docs.body: The primary region is us-east-1 with a warm standby in eu-west-1. Database replication is asynchronous, giving an RPO of about one minute and a target RTO of 30 minutes. Failover is manual and requires approval from the incident commander. DNS is switched via Route 53 health checks.

docs.title: Meeting: pricing change for the starter plan
docs.body: Leadership agreed to raise the Starter plan from 19 to 24 per seat for new customers from July 1. Existing customers keep their price for twelve months. Marketing will announce it two weeks in advance and support gets an FAQ. Churn will be reviewed monthly.

docs.title: Meeting: GDPR data deletion requests
docs.body: Legal confirmed that deletion requests must be completed within 30 days. Today the process is a manual script run by an engineer. We will build a self-service deletion flow that also purges backups after their 35-day retention window. Owner: Fatima from the privacy team.

docs.title: Incident: duplicate charges after retry storm
docs.body: On May 3 roughly 300 customers were charged twice. A timeout in the payment service caused clients to retry, and the charge endpoint was not idempotent. Refunds were issued the same day. Fix: require an Idempotency-Key header on charge requests and deduplicate on it for 24 hours.

docs.title: Tech debt: migrate CI from Jenkins to GitHub Actions
docs.body: Jenkins agents are hand-maintained and builds queue for up to twenty minutes at peak. We will move pipelines to GitHub Actions with self-hosted runners for the large integration suite. Order: libraries first, then services, then the monorepo. Target completion before Q4.

docs.title: Observability standards
docs.body: Every service must emit structured JSON logs with a request ID, expose Prometheus metrics for request rate, errors and duration, and propagate OpenTelemetry trace context. Dashboards follow the RED method. Alerts must link to a runbook.

docs.title: Decision: adopt TypeScript strict mode
docs.body: The frontend codebase will enable strict mode in tsconfig. New files must compile cleanly; existing files are migrated module by module with a temporary allowlist. The goal is to catch null-reference bugs that caused three production incidents last quarter.

docs.title: Customer feedback summary: dashboard
docs.body: Across 40 interviews, customers asked most often for saved filters, faster load times on large accounts, and scheduled email reports. Several enterprise admins want role-based access to dashboards. Dark mode was requested less than expected.

docs.title: Partnership: Initech reseller agreement
docs.body: Initech will resell our product in the APAC region with a 20% margin. They handle first-line support in local languages; escalations come to our support team. The agreement runs for two years with a quarterly business review. Legal contact: Hiro.

docs.title: Runbook: restoring from database backup
docs.body: Nightly snapshots are kept for 35 days and point-in-time recovery is available for the last 7 days. To restore, create a new instance from the snapshot, verify row counts against the metrics dashboard, then switch the connection string through the config service. Never restore over the live instance.

docs.title: Meeting: Kubernetes upgrade to 1.30
docs.body: The platform team will upgrade clusters from 1.27 to 1.30 in two steps over March. Deprecated APIs must be removed from Helm charts first; the pluto tool lists them. Staging goes first, production a week later during the Tuesday maintenance window.

docs.title: Analytics: activation funnel findings
docs.body: Only 38% of trial sign-ups connect a data source in their first week, and those who do convert to paid at four times the rate. The biggest drop is the OAuth consent screen. Proposed experiments: a sample dataset for instant value and an email nudge on day two.

docs.title: Legal: open source license policy
docs.body: Permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0 and BSD are approved for all use. LGPL is allowed for dynamically linked libraries. GPL and AGPL dependencies require legal review before being added, because they can impose obligations on our distributed software.

docs.title: Support macro: password reset not received
docs.body: Ask the user to check spam and confirm the email address on the account. If the domain uses strict filtering, have their IT team allowlist our sending domain. As a last resort an admin can trigger a reset link from the admin console, which expires after one hour.

docs.title: Quarterly OKRs: platform team
docs.body: Objective: make deployments boring. Key results: deploy frequency from weekly to daily, change failure rate under 10%, mean time to recovery under one hour, and 100% of services on the standard Helm chart by the end of the quarter.
